description: Reader-facing micro-wiki for lightly mentioned historical people, families, clans, factions, institutions and events. The novel provides the trigger and reading context; an authoritative external historical source provides a concise 2–3 line historical explanation.

source_policy.rule: Never merge external historical facts into novel evidence.

novel_trigger.context: Why the reference matters at this point

wiki.summary: Two or three concise lines of salient historical context.

novel_trigger.context: Historical commander referenced in the Sekigahara aftermath.

wiki.summary: Daimyo who commanded a major contingent of the Western Army at Sekigahara. His defection during the battle and attack on Otani Yoshitsugu's forces helped secure Tokugawa victory.

novel_trigger.context: Principal Western Army commander referenced in the Sekigahara context.

wiki.summary: Toyotomi administrator and leading commander of the Western coalition at Sekigahara. He was one of the principal political and military opponents of Tokugawa Ieyasu.

novel_trigger.context: Major Western Army commander referenced in the Sekigahara aftermath.

wiki.summary: Daimyo and major Toyotomi ally who commanded a large Western Army contingent at Sekigahara. He was one of the most prominent commanders on the losing side.

novel_trigger.context: Western Army commander referenced in the Sekigahara context.

wiki.summary: Daimyo of Satsuma and commander of the Shimazu contingent at Sekigahara. His troops were part of the Western Army during the decisive battle.

novel_trigger.context: Western Army commander referenced in the Sekigahara context.

wiki.summary: Christian daimyo and Toyotomi commander who fought for the Western Army at Sekigahara. He was among the principal commanders defeated in the battle.

novel_trigger.context: Leader of the victorious Eastern coalition at Sekigahara.

wiki.summary: Leader of the Eastern coalition at Sekigahara and the founder of the Tokugawa shogunate. His victory established the political order that dominated Japan for the following centuries.

novel_trigger.context: The battle whose immediate aftermath forms the opening setting of Book I.

wiki.summary: The decisive battle of 1600 between the Tokugawa-led Eastern coalition and the Western coalition associated with the Toyotomi cause. Tokugawa victory reshaped Japan's political order.
Coalition led by Tokugawa Ieyasu during the Sekigahara campaign. Its victory over the Western coalition established Tokugawa political dominance.
Coalition formed around the Toyotomi cause and opposed the Tokugawa-led Eastern Army at Sekigahara. Its defeat ended the immediate military challenge to Tokugawa power.
